question: Why do concurrent restores/copies grow from 100k to 10M docs, and how do glibc (+MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2, +MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=131072), jemalloc and mimalloc compare (glibc and musl builds)?

method.flags: --concurrency=8 --limit=5000; dump-sliced --slices=4; ~1 KB 'logs' docs from edgen seed 1

sizes.10000000: 2 reps (rep0, rep1); rep2 stopped to fit the box time budget -> dedicated load host

method.order: per rep: op -> variant, interleaved, so box stalls hit single runs rather than whole variants
method.peak_rss: child's own VmHWM sampled every 0.1 s (not wait4 ru_maxrss: Python starts children with vfork, so ru_maxrss includes the driver's own RSS; a /bin/true child of a 200 MB Python reported ~210 MB). measure.py/memcheck.py still use ru_maxrss (follow-up).
method.plateau: memcheck.py rule: peak after 50% of the run at most 10% above the peak before it
method.growth: median peak RSS at N vs median at 100k
method.throughput_note: 100k runs take <2 s with 0.1 s polling, so 100k docs/s is coarse; use 1M and 10M. Runs below 0.5x the median of all variants for that size/op are listed in throughput_outliers: they hit 6 different variants in single reps and did not repeat (box stalls on a shared host); the 10M musl/glibc-mmap128k restore (rep0 18-21k, rep1 65-66k) and glibc-arena2 copy (rep0 19k, rep1 58k) are such stalls.
method.gates_during_bench: gates ran pinned to CPUs 6-7 (nice 19) during part of the 100k/1M run; the 1M musl restore 11.5k outlier happened before they started

binaries.gnu: cargo build --release (fat LTO) x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, default / --features jemalloc / --features mimalloc, code identical to WIP 07ac51f (release_excess fix does not change these workloads: no document above the 4 MiB floor)
binaries.musl: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl built in the Dockerfile's pinned builder dhi.io/rust:1.99.0-alpine3.23-dev (rustc 1.99.0; apk make perl added for jemalloc), run through the builder's ld-musl-x86_64.so.1

root_cause.summary: No leak. Restore growth is glibc malloc retention/fragmentation (heap flat, RSS grows); copy growth is the bounded bufferSize queues filling once (bounded, plateaus) plus the same glibc retention.
root_cause.heaptrack_restore: c8 l5000: peak heap 183.9 MB at 100k vs 184.6 MB at 1M, heap per decile flat 164-174 MB; 91 leaked allocations (25.9 KB) at both sizes; RSS (with heaptrack) 248 -> 367 MB
root_cause.heaptrack_copy: heap 158.5 -> 246.5 MB, rises to ~229 MB by mid-run then flat; growth = extract.rs page buffers waiting in the processed channels (capacity bufferSize): 15 MB live at 100k (only 20 pages, queues never fill) vs 90 MB at 1M; with --bufferSize=4 30 MB / heap 183 MB; bulk.rs encoded buffers 88-89 MB at both sizes; leaks 104-106 allocations (28-35 KB)
root_cause.glibc_mechanism: buffers are allocated on worker threads and freed on sink threads; glibc's dynamic mmap threshold rises after the first large mmapped free (up to 32 MB), so later multi-MB buffers come from per-thread arenas and are retained. MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=131072 fixes the threshold (large buffers always mmapped/munmapped) and RSS stays flat; musl mallocng behaves the same way.
root_cause.never_shrinking_buffers: ValueSplitter.buf (JSON input splitter) and the --sourceOnly FileSink scratch buffer kept their largest capacity forever after one outsized document: fixed

code_fix.change: release_excess(): when a reused buffer's capacity is more than 2x max(4 MiB, 2x its length) it is shrunk to that size; called after ValueSplitter::compact(), after the eof-scalar clear, and after each FileSink sourceOnly batch

features.default: unchanged ([encrypted-keys]); both features together is a compile_error
features.deny_vet: deny.toml build-script allow entries, supply-chain/config.toml exemptions, docs/SUPPLY-CHAIN.md section

architectures.how: cargo zigbuild, toolchain 1.85.1 (release.yml's), --locked, LTO off; x86_64 run natively, aarch64 under qemu-aarch64 user mode (gnu with -L /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu); allocator symbols present in each feature build; x86_64-musl also built in the DHI Alpine builder (rustc 1.99.0) for all three
not_verified: native arm64 image builds (Dockerfile has no --platform)
Debian glibc builder images (make image-dhi-debian / image-public)
aarch64 kernels with 16K/64K pages: jemalloc built for 4K pages may fail there (JEMALLOC_SYS_WITH_LG_PAGE); mimalloc detects the page size at run time
enabling jemalloc in the Alpine image builder needs make (apk add make)

recommendation.decision: owner; nothing changed (default allocator, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX, src/memplan.rs and the README formula untouched)
text: Throughput is the same for every allocator on restore/copy (1M medians 64-75k restore, 54-63k copy; 10M rep1 65-68k / 55-60k). Plain dumps on musl and glibc-mmap128k are 15-20% slower (136-144k vs 149-178k d/s); sliced dumps the same.

Lowest and flattest memory: musl default and glibc+MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=131072 (restore 154/158 MB at 10M, +2%/+4% vs 100k, within the 10% goal; copy 222/226 MB, flat from 1M (+0-1%) but +61-64% vs 100k because of queue warm-up).

mimalloc is the best of the third-party allocators: same speed, restore 365 MB at 10M (+17% vs 100k, -30% vs glibc default), copy 419 MB (+51%, -39% vs glibc), plateau OK, builds and runs on all four targets. But it uses 2.3x (restore) / 1.9x (copy) / 7x (dump) the memory of the shipped musl build and of glibc-mmap128k, and more than glibc default on dumps (131 vs 75 MB; sliced 212 vs 165 MB).
jemalloc: same speed, restore 331 MB / copy 473 MB at 10M, still grows (+58% / +107%); 16K/64K-page aarch64 risk.

Suggested: keep musl's allocator for the release binaries and default image (do not switch them to mimalloc: it would raise memory). For glibc builds the cheapest fix is MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=131072 (env, or mallopt at start), costing 15-20% on plain dumps only; if one compiled-in allocator with the same behaviour on every libc is preferred, mimalloc is the choice over jemalloc, at about 2x musl's memory.

No variant meets 'copy within 10% from 100k to 10M': copy growth from 100k is the bufferSize queues filling once (bounded); a plateau- or 1M->10M-based criterion would pass for every variant except glibc default/jemalloc.
